note: Human-readable release notes the desktop shows in Settings → Advanced → Version. Newest first. Set "critical": true on a release that fixes data loss, a security issue, or a breaking sync change so it is called out prominently and the desktop can nudge harder.

entries.headline: Meetings: honest video frames, camera flip, real fullscreen, and room votes
notes: Your row and the Stage now show each camera's whole broadcast frame — exactly what a recording captures — instead of a crop.
Switch between front and back cameras with the new flip button (appears when your device has both).
The tile button is now a real fullscreen button: one press fills your screen, Esc or a second press exits.
Recordings carry a burned-in 'Recording — name' badge on the recorder's own panel, so a shared file always shows who made it.
New Vote menu: vote someone onto the stage, off the stage, or out of the room. One vote per person, majorities decide, and your stage votes are withdrawn automatically when you leave.
Meeting monitors and locked test rooms aside: this release also carries the 0.8.2 door-stability fixes for anyone who skipped it.

entries.headline: Meeting stability: a relay blip can no longer tear a room in two
notes: Meeting greeters now re-register the instant their relay socket reconnects (plus an idle keepalive and a zombie-socket watchdog), so a relay hiccup no longer leaves the room's door unmanned for minutes. Before this, a joiner in that window could stall at 'participants: 1' or accidentally found a second copy of the meeting — the split-room picker and the bouncing participant counts some rooms saw.
Meeting diagnostics now show when a participant's media is arriving via a friend-relay instead of a direct connection.

entries.headline: First public release
notes: Every app is a real animated GIF you own — drop it on your Home Screen and it runs, and sharing the file shares the whole app with its saved data inside.
Peer-to-peer Meetings that scale to large rooms on a self-healing mesh, with no server in the middle — and you can run any app live inside a meeting.
Any app goes multiplayer with one invite link (direct WebRTC, relay fallback); the link is yours by a secret only your app holds.
Fully offline-capable: your computer and its apps run in airplane mode. Back up a whole computer as one GIF and boot it anywhere.
Ten themed computers (the numbered subdomains), provenance signing, and per-person AI/API keys that apps can use but never see.
Two-player games (Tic-Tac-Toe, Connect Four) ask before New game clears the board — the other player consents, or you confirm your own reset.
Version panel: pin or roll back to any release. Switching a build rebuilds the built-in default apps to that build, and the data saved inside them carries over.
